svg.title: Chisum: Main switchboard, 690 V, JS8-865 revision 0
svg.text: Main switchboard, 690 V: the board, its one-line diagram, its panels · JS8-865 · revision 0 · 12 November 2026
Sheet 1 of 2. Nine cubicles on the place marked MSB in the main switchboard room, on the platform. Drawn before it is built.
Seen from the aisle, looking forward: outboard (port) is on the left.
Each cubicle 0.50 m wide, 0.80 m deep, 2.00 m high on a plinth of 0.10 m. Top door: instruments and lamps. Middle: the air circuit
breaker, drawn out to the front. Bottom door: the cables' terminals. Generator panels: ammeter, voltmeter, kilowatt meter; closed and open
lamps. Tie panel: synchroscope, double voltmeter, double frequency meter, three earth-fault lamps. The mimic painted across the doors:
blue, bars B; red, bars A; amber, the thruster bars. The cables come down into each cubicle from the trays over it.
No. 1 outboard, No. 9 inboard. It looks aft, into the aisle.
After row: the 440 V and 230 V sections (sheet 2)
It looks forward, into the same aisle.
T1, T2: the two transformers, 690/440 V, 800 kVA
At the outboard end of the room.
Behind the 690 V board: 0.80 m. Behind the after row: 0.60 m.
On the platform, 4.0 m above the keel.
Cable trays at 6.45 m: 0.35 m over the boards.
ONE-LINE DIAGRAM OF THE 690 V BOARD

· Bars A and bars B are tied in normal service; the three diesel sets run in parallel on them. Each is brought on at the synchronising panel (cubicle 5): voltages and frequencies matched, the breaker closed as the synchroscope comes to twelve o'clock.

· A shaft generator's frequency is its main engine's speed. It is not run in parallel with the diesel sets or with the other shaft generator, except for the seconds of a load transfer: an interlock between the breakers keeps it so.

· Manoeuvring: the thruster bus tie open, shaft generator No. 1 alone on the thruster bars with the thruster; the diesel sets on bars A and B. At sea: one shaft generator on the main bars through the thruster bus tie (SG1) or directly (SG2), the diesel
· Everything but the thruster takes its power at 440 V or 230 V through transformers No. 1 and No. 2 (sheet 2). Either transformer carries the whole of it.

· Three-wire, insulated from the hull: the three earth-fault lamps on cubicle 5 burn evenly while no line touches the hull. Not calculated, and owed: the short-circuit level of the bars (JS8-853) and the voltage dip when the thruster starts.
Shaft generator No. 2, engine room, starboard gear
Generating set No. 3, auxiliary engine room
Generating set No. 2, auxiliary engine room
